messages:
maya: FYI seeing a spike in 5xx and client timeouts from the canary group after the 03:12 deploy. Not wide yet but noisy.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: increased error rate on /v1/generate for shard r-12. Trigger: 5xx_rate > 3% for 2m. Paging on-call: @samir.
maya: tagging the canary id here: canary-2026-03-15-3. Routes show ~30% of traffic landing on it.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy canary-2026-03-15-3 started at 1710000732, cohorts: r-10,r-11,r-12. Health checks OK at deploy time.
samir: on it, jumping in — what's the symptom? increased latency or straight 5xx?
maya: mostly 502/504s and a few 500s. Latency for affected requests is ~1.8s before failing.
alex: looking at logs for r-12 — I see tokenizer OOM warnings interleaved with a new model variant load: model-redwood-v2-lite-quant. A handful of host processes spiked memory around the same time.
priya: could be a quantized kernel regression. We rolled a kernel patch in the build that the canary consumes.
jordan: customers reported errors to support—ticket count up 4x in last 10m for customers using streaming endpoints. Notified CSM.
ops-logger: customer-impact: 3 customers (acct-101, acct-442, acct-889) experiencing degraded responses; total affected requests ~3.2k in last 10m.
samir: ok immediate plan: 1) cut traffic to canary, 2) if errors persist, flip kill-switch for feature flag `model_variant_v2_switch`, 3) prepare single-commit revert patch if kill-switch not sufficient. Who can cut canary traffic?
maya: I can change routing weight. Reducing canary to 0% now.
maya: `routing set-weight canary-2026-03-15-3 0` -> accepted.
deploy-bot: Routing update: canary-2026-03-15-3 weight set to 0% across regions (applied by maya).
alex: after weight drop, errors dropped ~60% in r-12 within one minute but still some residual 5xx from hosts that had loaded the kernel.
priya: sounds like kernel regression + hot processes still serving the bad binary. We should trigger graceful restart of affected hosts, or flip feature flag to route away from new kernel path. Kill-switch first?
samir: flip the feature flag `model_variant_v2_switch` to false to force fallback to stable quant kernel. Priya, can you confirm the flag name and safety?
priya: confirmed flag: `model_variant_v2_switch`. Toggling is safe — fallback is the stable build. Doing the flip now.
priya: `feature-flag set model_variant_v2_switch false --env prod` -> queued.
incident-bot: Feature flag update recorded: model_variant_v2_switch = false (actor: priya).
alex: seeing immediate drop in OOMs on hosts that have reloaded. 5xx rate back to baseline 0.4% cluster-wide.
maya: support update drafted: "We identified an issue in a recent model kernel optimization in the canary cohort; we've disabled the variant and applied mitigations. If you continue to see issues, please reply to the ticket." Jordan please send.
jordan: sending now to affected CSMs and customers (acct-101, acct-442, acct-889).
samir: should we rollback the commit or just let hosts cycle and leave flag off? We need a hotfix for the build to avoid recurrence on next deploy.
priya: we should cut a single-commit hotpatch that reverts the kernel change; easier than a full rollback. I can prepare the revert PR and a canary.
maya: prioritize the hotpatch. Priya, can you include a minimal helm restart plan? We should avoid a mass restart.
priya: yes — I'll cherry-pick the revert commit `c7f9d2a` into a hotfix branch, run unit smoke, and then deploy a small canary to r-10 only at 5% before ramp.
priya: creating branch `hotfix/revert-kernel-2026-03-15` and opening PR now. Link: https://git.internal/r/repo/pulls/7123 (internal).
alex: while that builds, we should cordon and gracefully restart the few hosts that show OOMs to flush bad binary. I'll run rolling restarts on r-12 nodes with `drain` then `restart` at 30s stagger.
alex: commands: 
```
for node in $(list-nodes --shard r-12 --filter oom); do
  k8s drain $node --ignore-daemonsets && sleep 30 && k8s restart $node;
done
```
alex: executed for 3 nodes, all came back healthy.
ops-logger: post-action metrics: 5xx rate cluster-wide 0.18% (baseline ~0.2%), tail latency normalized.
samir: good job. Assigning follow-ups: Priya — hotfix PR + canary plan (due in 25m). Alex — confirm all affected hosts restarted and add a note of exact host ids (due in 15m). Jordan — customer comms sent and monitor. Maya — update runbook with toggle details. I'll draft an incident summary and set up a short bridge.
maya: joining bridge: zoom.redwood/incident-29765.
incident-bot: Incident severity set to Sev2 (customer-impacting degraded performance) by samir.
priya: PR created and tests green. Running canary deploy to r-10 at 5%.
deploy-bot: Canary hotfix-deploy hotfix/revert-kernel-2026-03-15 -> r-10 weight 5% starting.
priya: canary metrics look clean for 10m. No OOMs, 5xx at 0.1%. Requesting ramp to 30% then full.
samir: approve ramp. Priya ramp to 30% then monitor 10m.
priya: ramped to 30%. Monitoring.
ops-logger: 20m after hotfix: cluster stable, no new OOMs, error queues normal.
maya: closing immediate paging loop — will keep thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
samir: thanks all. We'll run a short postmortem tomorrow. Priya please include root cause hypothesis: kernel regression in quantized path + canary routing that exposed residual processes; mitigation was feature-flag disable + host restarts + single-commit revert.
priya: agreed. I'll include timeline, impact numbers, and remediation steps in the postmortem doc.
incident-bot: Incident resolved by samir. Incident closed at 2976543425.
